C-001.reasoning: Caption reads United States District Court for the Eastern District of Tennessee at Greeneville.

C-003.reasoning: Caption lists Dr. Nathan J. Vogler et al. as Plaintiffs and Crestline Health Systems, Inc. as Defendant.

C-004.reasoning: Title is Memorandum of Law in Support of Defendant's Motion to Dismiss under Rule 12(b)(6).

C-005.reasoning: Both a table of contents and a table of authorities are included.

C-006.reasoning: The Introduction section never mentions Rule 12(b)(6) or the motion to dismiss; only the title and the Legal Standard/Conclusion do.

C-007.reasoning: Parts I, II, V and VI address dismissal of Count I monopolization.

C-008.reasoning: Part III specifically addresses Count II attempted monopolization.

C-009.reasoning: Part IV specifically addresses Count III under Section 1.

C-010.reasoning: Conclusion asks that the Verified Complaint be dismissed in its entirety with prejudice.

C-011.reasoning: Cites Twombly and Iqbal, facial plausibility and that conclusory recitals do not suffice.

C-012.reasoning: The memo deliberately does not argue that excluding government payers (44%) makes the market deficient; it only says the 70% figure is all-payer.

C-013.reasoning: No argument based on substitutability, hypothetical monopolist, or cross-elasticity regarding payer-type exclusion.

C-014.reasoning: Geographic market is challenged but no specific alternative area (Bristol/Abingdon, Asheville) is identified; only a generic reference to the nearby state line.

C-015.reasoning: The geographic market argument is not connected to inflating Crestline's market share.

C-016.reasoning: Memo states the over-60% revenue figure in para 83 cannot be squared with the approximately 70% figure in para 47.

C-017.reasoning: Argues the two inconsistent, undefined figures are not shares of the alleged market and cannot support monopoly power.

C-018.reasoning: The memo asserts no numerical threshold for inferring monopoly power, so the threshold is not discussed.

C-019.reasoning: Argues PPCAs are non-exclusive preferred tier pricing ($25 vs $75) and not exclusive dealing since insurers may contract with rivals.

C-020.reasoning: States the other seven Plaintiffs remain in-network with at least one of the three major insurers, undercutting foreclosure.

C-021.reasoning: Argues only competitor revenue harm is alleged, no higher prices, lower output or quality, and cites competition-not-competitors.

C-022.reasoning: Cites Brunswick for antitrust injury and competition not competitors.

C-023.reasoning: Part IV states the PPCAs are vertical and judged under the rule of reason.

C-024.reasoning: Cites Leegin, 551 U.S. 877, for rule of reason treatment of vertical restraints.

C-025.reasoning: States no horizontal agreement among competitors is alleged and the PPCAs are vertical provider-customer agreements.

C-026.reasoning: Argues intent allegations are inferences from PPCA structure/timing and para 82 identifies no document, statement, meeting or communication.

C-027.reasoning: Argues the facts describe a seller winning buyers with a better price, which is not specific intent to monopolize.

C-028.reasoning: Cites Spectrum Sports for the three elements of attempted monopolization.

C-029.reasoning: Argues the 22% discount is passed on to members as lower cost-sharing and the Complaint pleads no consumer harm under the rule of reason.

C-030.reasoning: Argues year-to-year renewals and 180-day at-will termination negate foreclosure.

C-031.reasoning: Cites Tampa Electric, Omega, CDC Technologies and Concord Boat on duration/terminability.

C-032.reasoning: Part VI raises AGC efficient-enforcer factors, noting Plaintiffs are not PPCA parties and AMP is not a plaintiff.

C-033.reasoning: The memo deliberately omits the independent surgeons holding Tier 1 status argument.

C-034.reasoning: The appended drafting notes in the memorandum document reference Ledger & Thorne and its data by name multiple times.

C-035.reasoning: The appended drafting notes reference the Beale email and Mr. Beale's account of the network removals.

C-036.reasoning: Motion is expressly brought under Fed. R. Civ. P. 12(b)(6).

C-037.reasoning: States monopoly power in relevant market and willful acquisition/maintenance distinguished from superior product etc. (Grinnell).

C-038.reasoning: Lists anticompetitive conduct, specific intent, and dangerous probability citing Spectrum Sports.

C-039.reasoning: States only an agreement that unreasonably restrains trade; the interstate commerce element is omitted.

C-040.reasoning: Body facts are cited to the Complaint and the Blue Ridgeway PPCA; extrinsic data is expressly excluded.

C-041.reasoning: Body from Introduction to Conclusion is about 6,150 words, with the argument well over 4,000 words.

C-042.reasoning: Part III argues dangerous probability fails for market-definition reasons in Part II and non-exclusive terminable PPCAs.

C-043.reasoning: Part I.C argues the 82.5% covered-lives figure is not foreclosure and preferential tiering does not foreclose a substantial share.
